Goals and boundaries

The main target is Junior Backend Developer with Go, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Docker, Git, testing and Linux. Python and AI are supporting paths; architecture and GPU topics lay foundations for later specialization. Completing 26 weeks guarantees neither AI/GPU expertise nor employment. Go targets an intermediate practical level; React and TypeScript support simple interfaces, and C builds memory understanding.
26 weeks, 390 hours

Weeks 1–24 form the main six-month path. Week 25 closes gaps and week 26 covers assessment and portfolio work as additional structure. Each week has 480 backend minutes, 180 AI minutes, 120 systems minutes and 120 project/review minutes. Related practice is counted in its own path, not again in projects. The optional CUDA experiment is outside the core time and denominator. At 10 hours per week the content takes about 39 weeks, and at 8 hours about 49 weeks; this is more precise than the original approximate nine-month recommendation.
How to study and use AI

First read or watch the lesson, rewrite the example without looking, do a small exercise and produce independent work at the end of the week. Define the problem and inputs/outputs yourself first. Ask AI for solutions and reasons, keeping each task small. Understand generated code line by line, check possible errors and data movement, and test and debug it yourself. You should be able to explain and change the code and accept technical responsibility for it.
Correcting the epoch explanation

The original text asked why a model improves with every epoch. That assumption has been corrected: decreasing training loss or increasing epochs does not guarantee higher validation/test accuracy. Overfitting, noise and learning rate can worsen results; inspect training and validation separately and reserve test data for final evaluation.
Measure your hardware

An RTX 3060 with 6 GB VRAM is only an assumption in the original roadmap, not a confirmed specification of your device. Before choosing a model, inspect and measure the device, free RAM/VRAM, dtype, sequence length, batch size, activations and optimizer memory. Quantization, LoRA/QLoRA and mixed precision do not guarantee any model will fit. Choose small models and datasets on CPU; for cloud GPUs/Colab, check compatibility, access, quotas, cost and privacy at the time of use. No GPU does not prevent the Backend path or small MNIST work on CPU.
StudioFlow AI scope

StudioFlow is an educational animation-production management project: projects, sequences, shots, tasks, teams, roles, status, file versions, deadlines and a dashboard. The first AI feature only summarizes shot descriptions. Tag suggestions, task generation from descriptions and text-file/production-report analysis are alternatives from the original text, not simultaneous requirements. A pretrained model or API can be used; training an LLM from scratch is unnecessary. Do not send real production data to an external service without an explicit action and permission.
Read resources selectively

The original priorities are A Tour of Go, Go Tutorials, SQLBolt, PostgreSQL, Docker Get Started, React Learn, PyTorch Basics, Hugging Face, Nand2Tetris, the CUDA Guide, CS:APP and OSTEP. Its additional sources—Go by Example, the Python Tutorial, ML Crash Course, JavaScript.info, the TypeScript Handbook and the fine-tuning guide—are also in the library. You do not need to finish all of Nand2Tetris/CS:APP/OSTEP; follow only the week's relevant topic. Opening a link is not equivalent to studying or mastery.
Career paths and continuing

Go Backend Developer and Junior Software Engineer in backend work are the main targets; a listing in another language requires learning that language too. Full-stack work requires independent React/TypeScript interface skills. AI Application Developer needs Python, APIs, evaluation and then embeddings/RAG. ML Engineer requires more mathematics, statistics, algorithms and data experience; only some introductory internships may be relevant now. GPU/CUDA and Computer Architecture Engineer are long-term goals requiring C/C++, architecture and memory optimization.
After this path

Backend/Distributed Systems: distributed services, cloud, databases and scalability. AI Infrastructure: model serving, GPU management, memory and inference speed, combining Backend/Systems/AI. ML Engineering: Python, mathematics, model training and deployment. GPU/Systems: C/C++, CUDA, kernels and memory. Do not add Rust to the load during these six months; after Go and systems fundamentals, it becomes a more deliberate choice.
